author: lernie
text:
terminal compaction stub + no-ff merge back

Completes v0.2 task bl-8c66: lernie prompt now runs the full
§2.3+§2.6+§2.7 lifecycle. After the response commit, the harness
dispatches the terminal compactor off the exchange tip (§2.7), which
spawns inv/<ex-id>/<cmp-id>, writes .agent/compactions/001.md with
a one-line summary ('exchange <id>: <response-text>'), commits it,
and --no-ff merges back into the exchange branch. The exchange
branch then rebases onto main and --no-ff merges in. Worktrees are
removed; branch refs survive for the retention window (§2.3).

The compactor is a v0.2 stub: no model call, mark_for_deletion is a
no-op. The dispatch shape is what ships — spawn-on-own-branch,
write, merge-back through the same rebase_and_merge helper used for
the ex→main path. That shared helper is the 'One obvious path'
principle in code (new principle added to docs/PRINCIPLES.md).

CLI: added 'lernie dispatch compactor <repo> <branch>', the same
CLI surface the in-process caller uses (§3.4).

Docs: refreshed ARCH §2.3/§12 to mark v0.2 merge-back landed,
expanded ARCH §2.5 with a paragraph explaining why the git-oriented
architecture collapses compaction/verification/parsing-dispatch onto
one primitive, updated README prompt walkthrough end-to-end.
